selection_basis: aggregate Gate F evidence plus frozen Candidate-v6 design only

architectures.name: STRICT_V6_PLUS_GENERIC_EVIDENCE_FALLBACK
risks: fallback semantics can become an unprincipled lexical acceptor unless hard rejection and compatibility rules are explicit

architectures.name: RELAXED_STRUCTURAL_ASSERTION_PARSER
risks: still turns open-domain evidence into a parser-coverage problem

architectures.name: RETRIEVAL_CONFIDENCE_ABSTENTION_GATE
risks: retrieval confidence is not evidence entailment
may weaken no-evidence safety and conflate ranking with answerability

architectures.name: HYBRID_TYPED_PLUS_GENERIC_LEXICAL_ENTAILMENT
strengths: strict structural verifier remains a high-precision path
generic deterministic evidence compatibility addresses heterogeneous natural language
hard rejection can preserve explicit absence/non-assertion/contradiction safety
Candidate-v2 ranking can remain frozen and unchanged
risks: generic lexical entailment must be bounded to direct factual specificity
synonym/cue families can overfit if derived from protected/final cases

selection_rationale: Gate F demonstrates an extreme coverage/safety split: Candidate-v6 rejects all answerable cases while correctly abstaining on all no-evidence cases. Architecture D preserves the typed strict path as a precision mechanism, adds a benchmark-agnostic deterministic compatibility path for natural-language factual evidence, and keeps contradiction/absence/non-assertion as hard rejects. It also cleanly separates answerability verification from the frozen Candidate-v2 ranking backend.
